# E4 — the fast refresh: can the profile be refreshed without running the program again, and can the model's own report of the dependences close what that leaves open?

*Generated by `agent/tools/campaign.py reports` from `results/campaign.json` and the experiment record (`agent/THESIS_EXPERIMENTS.md`). Edit those, then regenerate — not this file.*

**Status:** running

## The question

After the model has rewritten a loop, the agent profiles the whole program again; the fast refresh compiles only and carries the last run's dependences over, so the code the model just wrote has no measurement. Does that change whether the agent keeps a rewrite (H6's second half), does the model's own report of the dependences of its new lines repair it (H7), is adding dependences safe where deleting them is not (H7b) — and how many seconds does one refresh save where the run is long? In four steps, the cheap ones first (the author, 12 Oct): (1) the saved rewrites of the model replayed without a model, (2) the model's report on the rewrites that differ, (3) the time on programs with a long run, (4) live trials only if steps 1 and 2 say the refresh keeps DiscoPoP's verdicts. (RQ6, RQ7, C3)

## Result in one paragraph

Open again (13 Oct, late — the author: "run both", after it had been closed the same evening): steps 1 to 3 are read out, and the live trials (step 4) are run after all, on the 18 loops as the reference and on a benchmark whose profiling run is long — the only place a refresh can save time (his rule of 26 Sep); that benchmark is being fixed without a model, and nothing is launched before he has seen it with its cost. What steps 1 to 3 say: the fast refresh changes whether the agent keeps a rewrite on 58 of 599 saved rewrites and throws away 22 wins, saves nothing on the 18 loops and 1.5 to 7.5 % of an agent trial where the profiling run is long; the model's own report of the dependences, as the agent uses it, does not rescue it; and that deleting dependences is unsafe where adding them is not could not be measured. The model is not asked on all 599 rewrites and the agent is unchanged (his decisions of 13 Oct, which stand). In detail — Step 1 is read out (12 Oct; `e4_replay`, no model, 33 minutes on the server): 599 of the 601 pragma-free rewrites that passed the checks in the trials of E1-v6, E3 and E3b were judged after a fast refresh, after a full re-profile and after a second full re-profile as the control. The fast refresh changes whether the agent keeps the rewrite in 58 of 599, the control in 0 — the registered test E4-1: p = 0.000326, at most 0.0176 in the campaign's family of 54: H6's second half is refuted. 22 rewrites are kept only after the full re-profile — 20 of them loops the model turned into a reduction, for which the fast refresh makes DiscoPoP write `firstprivate` of the accumulator, a directive the agent's clause check refuses — and 13 of the 22 are rewrites their trial shipped; 2 are kept only after the fast refresh; 34 are kept after both with other directives, 27 of those differing only in a redundant `shared` clause (counted as the same, not registered: 31 differ, p = 0.000977, bound 0.0527). DiscoPoP's verdict on the rewritten lines differs in 417 of 599 (control 0). No time is saved on these loops: one refresh 1.54 s against 1.75 s, and with the gate's checks on the extra directives 1,758 s against 1,730 s in total. Step 3 is read out (12 Oct; `e4_refresh_time`, no model): where the profiling run is long one fast refresh saves 36 s on `hotspot` (33 % of a full re-profile; the explorer's own time there moves between 52 and 129 s), 27 s on `is` (66 %), 21.5 s on `md` (63 %) and 4.2 s on `correlation` (54 %) — 1.5 to 7.5 % of an agent trial on those programs — and on an unchanged program its Do-All and reduction loops are those of a full profile. Step 2 is prepared without a model: a hand-written correct report gives DiscoPoP the reduction back on three of the lost rewrites (a minimum, a sum, a maximum), and the dry pass `e4_report_dry` shows a run over all 599 rewrites sends 599 report requests while the deletion review has something to ask on 21 rewrites only, none among the 58 that differ; the fast refresh repeats itself on 599 of 599. Step 2 is read out (13 Oct; `e4_report_a`, the author's "ok" for the smaller set; 136 Haiku calls, $8.53): the model's report gives back 20 of the 22 lost wins (all 20 reductions) and removes both keeps the full profile does not make, but changes 11 of the 58 drawn rewrites that the fast refresh had right — about 102 of the 541 (at least 60 at 95 %), more than the 28 it repairs: H7 is not refuted on the selected set and fails on the population; in all of the damaged rewrites the reply calls the loop independent — the agent places a reported dependence without its loop. The deletion changed no decision on its 21 rewrites: H7b is refuted as registered (0 against 0). A what-if on the saved replies (`e4_report_a_placement`, no model): placed again as built they give the recorded decisions on 116 of 116; with claims left out where they lie inside a loop the reply calls independent, the 5 wins the report cost come back, 3 of the 20 regained reductions are lost again and one keep the full profile does not make returns — not a repair.

The question the saved replies can answer without a model: how much of the damage disappears if a reported dependence is not allowed to count against a loop the same reply calls independent — and what that costs. **What runs** (`report_replay.py --report replay --replies …/runs/e4_report_a`, at the commit that holds this row): for each of the 116 rewrites the profile before, the fast refresh, then the reply recorded in `e4_report_a` placed again and the rewrite judged again, and the full re-profile — twice: (a) `--placement as-built`, the agent's own placing: a control, which must give `e4_report_a`'s decisions again; where it does not, that is the pipeline's own variation; (b) `--placement respect-none`: every claimed dependence is left out whose two lines both lie inside a loop that the same reply declares independent (`LOOP <line> NONE`; the loop's extent by brace balance, the agent's `_loop_span`). **What the rule is and is not.** It discards claims; it does not move them to their loop. Moving a claim to its loop was not attempted: the agent's rows carry no run-time context (DiscoPoP's own rows carry a callpath state), and in these replays a row counted against the loops around both of its lines; whether a row can be given the context of one loop was not examined. Leaving a claim out is the lever that needs no change to the dependence data. It is therefore an upper bound on what a better placing would give back, and it can itself drop a true dependence of an outer loop; nothing becomes less safe than after the fast refresh alone only because those loops were already offered there and are judged by the same checks. It leans on the model's 'independent', which the agent as built only logs. **Chosen after the data were seen:** the rule was picked once it was known which rewrites broke. Tried while the main run was going on seven rewrites on the Mac (with the replies recorded up to then): the tool works; on two rewrites whose clause changed (`shared` to `firstprivate`) the rule left the claims inside the independent loops out and the clause still changed, because dependences that link two sibling loops remain. **Read out:** the tables of the main read-out for each placing; rewrite by rewrite, the as-built replay against `e4_report_a` and the what-if against the as-built replay; claims left out. **Expected:** the control reproduces `e4_report_a` on all or nearly all of the 116; with the rule the 20 reductions stay repaired, most of the 5 wins the report lost come back, the clause changes mostly stay. **What it cannot decide:** whether the placing is changed in the agent — that is a change to the agent and the author's.
